sources.excerpt: Official Chick-fil-A homepage identifies the national chain and currently promotes Honey Pepper Pimento, Peach treats, Pineapple Dragonfruit beverages, and the Mac & Cheese Kid?s Meal.
Official national menu landing page covering breakfast, entr?es, salads, sides, beverages, treats, Kid?s Meals, Family Style Meals, and catering; price and availability may vary by location.
Official catering landing page covering trays, packaged meals, breakfast, entr?es, sides, treats, and nonalcoholic beverages; availability varies by location.

Live official nutrition/allergen system contained 174 top-level rows in 17 sections, consolidated to 162 unique current products. Contains flags cover milk, egg, soy, wheat, sesame, tree nuts, peanut, and fish.
Official FAQ directs guests to the Nutrition and Allergens page for common allergens and to individual menu-item ingredient sections.

Official FAQ says fully refined peanut oil is not considered a major allergen, but shared cooking/preparation areas and supplier variation mean food cannot be ensured allergen-free; wheat, egg, soy, and milk products are made in Chick-fil-A kitchens.
Current Creamy Salsa Dressing ingredient list includes egg yolk and contains no milk ingredient, agreeing with the live matrix?s Egg-only positive and conflicting with the frozen Milk positive.
Restaurant-controlled ordering system requires JavaScript and a selected restaurant before exposing a location-specific ordering menu; no independent chain-wide allergen matrix was exposed.

Targeted domain searches for allergen, allergy, nutrition, ingredients, PDF, and menu surfaced the official matrix, FAQs, current menu/product pages, and no higher-authority conflicting current document.

restaurantLevelAllergenEvidence.text: Chick-fil-A says shared cooking and preparation areas and supplier variation mean it cannot ensure food is free from allergens; wheat, egg, soy, and milk products are made in its kitchens. This is retained at restaurant level and not expanded into unsupported item-specific may-contain claims.

Chick-fil-A states its hand-breaded chicken is cooked in fully refined peanut oil and that highly refined peanut oil is not considered a major food allergen; no peanut positive is inferred from the cooking oil.

findings.summary: The frozen official projection lists Creamy Salsa Dressing as containing milk and egg. The live official matrix now marks Egg only and explicitly says ?Does not contain Milk?; the current official ingredient list contains egg yolk and no milk ingredient.

proposedChanges: Replace the 148-product frozen projection with the 162-product consolidated live official boundary; all 148 frozen products remain current and 14 products are net new.

Add Breakfast Breads, Iced Coffee, Catering Coffee, two regular Sunjoy diet-lemonade combinations, two Pineapple Dragonfruit Sunjoy diet-lemonade combinations, Zesty Apple Cider Vinaigrette, and six gallon beverage combinations.
Preserve only live explicit Contains flags from the eight-column official matrix; keep products with no positive flag unavailable rather than asserting absence.
Retain Chick-fil-A?s shared-kitchen and refined-peanut-oil disclosures at restaurant level without converting them into universal item-level may-contain claims.
Resolve the single Creamy Salsa Dressing historical Milk-positive versus current Egg-only official conflict; the current ingredient page corroborates the live matrix.
Remove 19 frozen direct gluten positives that were not explicit columns in the official matrix and therefore should not be represented as direct restaurant-issued allergen flags.
